title: Conditional ordered-limit rectangular-tail bridge
question: Can explicit uniform cutoff and volume tail bounds be composed in either declared order into one common rectangular-tail estimate before an owner-specific ordered limit is claimed?
decision_reason: The existing R-451/R-456 interfaces control history propagation and weighted recurrences but do not state the final epsilon bookkeeping for an ordered two-parameter limit. R-474 adds that missing contract without inventing a source owner, common norm, or physical candidate.
method: Freeze n as the cutoff/lattice index and m as the volume/exhaustion index, with separate intermediate observables B(m) and C(n).
Prove the cutoff-then-volume rectangle by splitting epsilon into two strict epsilon/2 tails and applying the triangle inequality.
Prove the volume-then-cutoff rectangle independently with the reversed intermediate observable.
Exercise the contract on an exact geometric fixture with bases two and three, deriving thresholds rather than inserting them.
Run a non-importing Fraction implementation, a ten-mutation hostile contract harness, the integrated verifier, and Lean R474.
Keep the result T0 claim-nonbearing and classify it as auxiliary support because all source-owned hypotheses remain open.
finding: The two epsilon-split implications compile in Lean and reproduce exactly in the primary and independent arithmetic lanes. The geometric fixture passes 40/40 primary assertions, 16/16 independent assertions, 10/10 hostile mutation rejections, and 13/13 integrated assertions. This closes only the abstract rectangle bookkeeping; it does not establish any owner-supplied tail or limit.
decision_scope: T0 conditional two-parameter epsilon bridge for a scalar common-norm placeholder; no TECT field, source dynamics, finite table, physical map, or infinite-limit data are instantiated.
evidence_level: T0 exact conditional epsilon bridge with independent, hostile, integrated and Lean checks
boundary: R-474 turns owner-supplied uniform tails into a rectangular-tail certificate. It does not prove the tails, identify the intermediate observables, or establish an ordered limit for TECT.
assumptions: A single already-declared common norm supports both triangle-inequality estimates.
The forward and reverse intermediate observables are fixed before evaluating the tails.
Strict epsilon/2 bounds are source-owner hypotheses, not consequences of the synthetic fixture.
The arithmetic fixture is a contract test only and is not an exhaustion surrogate.
missing_assumptions: A hash-pinned source-owned TECT functional and compatible microscopic generator or transfer.
A common invariant core and common norm for every regulator and volume.
Source-authorized cutoff-, lattice-, volume-, boundary-, phase- and beta-uniform tail estimates.
A proof that A, B and C are the same physical observable under the declared maps.
An ordered regulator-removal theorem, including existence or equivalence-class language.
Physical-sector projection and independent holdout observation correspondence.
non_claims: No source-owned dynamics, production functional, Q3 heat-root map or R-192 owner slot is supplied.
No common-core, uniform-estimate, thermodynamic, continuum, common-alpha, physical-sector, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity or mass-gap theorem is claimed.
Passing both order fixtures does not show that the actual TECT orders exist or agree.
No finite fixture is promoted to a physical prediction or Pre-A/Sector-A closure.

adversarial_review.check: Could epsilon/2 be replaced by an unsafe split or a non-strict bound?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: Lean and both lanes require a positive denominator two and strict inequalities.

adversarial_review.check: Could the forward and reverse orders be silently swapped?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: model order labels and hostile order mutation are checked.

adversarial_review.check: Could finite geometric rows be presented as source-uniform tails?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: fixture, source-owner and uniformity flags remain explicitly separate.

adversarial_review.check: Could absolute-value algebra be promoted to an operator-domain theorem?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: common norm and domain are listed as missing assumptions.

adversarial_review.check: Could the auxiliary result close T-054 or physical gates?
adversarial_review.disposition: REJECTED: claim-bearing is false, all downstream scope flags are false, and the next action requires a real owner packet.

next_action: When a non-synthetic owner packet exists, instantiate both order contracts in its declared common norm and prove source-, cutoff-, lattice-, volume-, phase- and beta-uniform tails before attempting the ordered limit. Until then keep T-054 at owner intake and do not repeat physical-empty tests.
stop_or_redesign: If either order needs a different norm, split the contract and record the incompatibility rather than taking a triangle inequality across norms.
If a tail is only non-strict or finite-sample, retain the fixture as diagnostic and do not call it uniform.
If the source owner changes an intermediate observable or limit order, issue a new versioned packet instead of mutating R-474.
If the owner packet is absent, preserve this conditional bridge as auxiliary support and leave the mainline gate open.
